claims.explanation: TWS-119 is a GSK3β inhibitor that activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling; selectivity likely reflects dependence on Wnt pathway activation for growth or survival, with TP53 loss and EGFR/BRAF activation cooperating to sensitize lines, while intact PTEN/PIK3CA-AKT signaling or NF1 loss provides protection. The strongest pattern is enrichment of TP53 mutations and EGFR/BRAF alterations among sensitive lines, consistent with GSK3 inhibition promoting β-catenin-driven proliferation in cells lacking p53-mediated checkpoints.

features.basis: Observed enrichment of TP53 mutations in sensitive lines; loss of p53 checkpoint may permit Wnt-driven proliferation
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) are among most sensitive; EGFR signaling cooperates with Wnt/β-catenin
BRAF-mutant lines (SNUC5, IGR37, K029AX, HEC265) appear in sensitive set; MAPK activation may synergize with GSK3 inhibition
PTEN-mutant lines (ZR751, FTC133, KALS1, UACC62, 786O) are enriched in least-affected set; PI3K/AKT activation may bypass GSK3 inhibition
NF1-mutant lines (S117, LOXIMVI, BICR6, KALS1, FTC133) appear in resistant set; RAS/MAPK activation may reduce dependence on GSK3
CTNNB1-mutant lines (HEC265, KE39) are sensitive; Wnt pathway activation may be required for TWS-119 effect
APC-mutant colorectal lines (SNUC5) sensitive; Wnt activation via APC loss may sensitize to GSK3 inhibition
PIK3CA-mutant lines (HGC27, MKN1, SNU410) are in resistant set; PI3K activation may compensate for GSK3 inhibition
KRAS-mutant lines (CL11, GSU, SNU410, OV7) appear in resistant set; RAS/MAPK activation may bypass GSK3 dependence
TWS-119 is a GSK3β inhibitor; higher GSK3B expression may indicate greater dependence on GSK3 activity
MYC is an annotated target; MYC-driven lines may depend on GSK3-mediated stabilization
JUN is an annotated target; AP-1 signaling may mediate sensitivity to GSK3 inhibition
